instruction: Using only the standalone learner-facing English stem, prompts, and opaque token pools, select exactly one condition, two actions, and two parameters. Return the required structured JSON, including exactly one premise row for every opaque token. Do not infer absent client-specific facts.
stem: Stage 3 synthesis: A post-operative client with CKD had a potassium of 3.1 mEq/L. A covering resident ordered potassium chloride 40 mEq in 100 mL normal saline to infuse through a peripheral IV over 1 hour, despite a unit protocol limiting peripheral potassium to 10 mEq/100 mL and 10 mEq/hr and requiring renal-function verification. The nurse questioned the order; the resident insisted it be run without addressing the protocol or eGFR 34 mL/min. The nurse used the chain of command, the unsafe order was not administered, and a revised order of 10 mEq in 100 mL over 1 hour was obtained. Complete the bow-tie diagram.

actions.label: A1
actions.text: Use structured assertive safety communication with the ordering provider

actions.label: A2
actions.text: Withhold the unsafe order and escalate through the chain of command

actions.label: A3
actions.text: Refuse the order and document, but do not pursue a safe replacement order

actions.label: A4
actions.text: Administer the potassium as originally ordered

condition.label: C1
condition.text: Unsafe medication order causing an interprofessional safety conflict

condition.label: C2
condition.text: Personality clash or poor bedside manner only

condition.label: C3
condition.text: Equivalent clinical-preference difference about potassium replacement

parameters.label: P2
parameters.text: Number of pages the resident is managing

parameters.label: P3
parameters.text: Potassium trend, cardiac rhythm, and IV-site tolerance during replacement

parameters.label: P4
parameters.text: Revised order is protocol-compliant and original unsafe order is not administered
